title: What If the Archduke's Driver Had Known the Way?
topic: What if Archduke Franz Ferdinand's driver had known the route? (Sarajevo, 28 June 1914)
mechanism: A route change nobody passed to the drivers sent the Archduke's car into a wrong turn at the Latin Bridge; reversing, it stood still right beside Gavrilo Princip, and the killing set off the alliance chain (Austria-Serbia-Russia-Germany-France) into World War One.

beats.hook: A driver took one wrong turn, and stopped right in front of an assassin: one continuous push from the river wall onto the green open car standing at the corner, a young man at the delicatessen door.
beats.but: That morning a bomb is thrown; it bounces off the folded top and blows up under the next car.
beats.then: The plot seems dead; Princip drifts to a street corner; the Archduke changes plans to visit the wounded.
beats.conflict: Nobody tells the drivers: the lead car turns down the old route, his driver follows, the governor shouts 'Wrong way! Stop!'; the car stops a few steps from Princip; two shots.
beats.pivot: You see, Austria blamed Serbia and declared war one month later; Russia, Germany and France fall in line like labelled dominoes on a map table.
beats.so: Within a week most of Europe was at war; a counter turns toward twenty million and four crowns topple. Now, what if the driver had known? The car speeds past the corner.
beats.closing: Would war have come anyway? Many historians think so, but not that day; it came down to one wrong turn.
